utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please, and good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Oric. You may sit down and good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, and also good morning to my learned friends of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with counsel Ms. Patricia Sellers, counsel Mr. Gramsci di Fazio, and our case manager, Mrs. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, good morning to my colleagues from the Prosecution. I am Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones, I represent Mr. Naser Oric. And we have our legal assistant with us, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. As soon as you have definitive developments following the Rule 70 motion, please brief us so that we can define the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, you would have received --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: From our part, we don't expect we will have any further communications to make. The ball is in the Prosecution's court as far as we are concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I'm saying as long as you -- as soon as you have a definitive position taken following the recent developments please let us know. All right? Bring the witness in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Malagic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are proceeding with your testimony today, as I explained yesterday. You don't need to reiterate the solemn declaration that you entered yesterday. You're still testifying on the basis of it. Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Malagic.

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We'll continue where we left off yesterday. Let me ask you first, I have a feeling that you have some problems with your headphones. Is everything all right now?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everything is all right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you were talking about the offensive at Pirici, Poloznik, and you told us that the population had left and then had returned to the area again, am I right?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask the usher to show the witness a document, a new document. It's a document by the command of the Drina Corps of the 12th of December, 1992. It's called a report on the -- on a team visit. And it's addressed to the command of the Bratunac Brigade, Colonel Milenko Zivanovic. First of all, could you please look at the document, and I would like to ask you whether you, in the second half of November 1992 or in early December 1992, heard anything about the existence of the Bratunac Brigade or found out about it in any way?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By listening in at Likari we found out about the establishment of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Malagic, I would like to read to you the first sentence of the second passage of this document. The goal of the visit, and it's obvious that this is pertaining to a tour of certain areas around Bratunac, so the drafter of the document says the goal of the visit was to analyse all aspects of the state of combat readiness of the commands and units focus being on command and control and logistics support. Then I would like to quote to you something from the fourth passage, and that is, the brigade was formed on the 14th of November 1992, in accordance with the envisaged establishment and was allotted its zone of operation. It was formed out of TO, Territorial Defence, units in the main detachment and units of the local communes. The problems of its formation need to be analysed in greater detail. And then paragraph 7 of the document. The brigade command is drawing up all necessary documents on the basis of which combat operations are successfully being directed. Shelters appropriate for living in combat operations in wintertime have been built but soldiers are ill-disposed to carrying out offensive operations or to being engaged outside of their allotted territory. Mr. Malagic, I would like to ask you a question about this. You said that you had found out about the establishment of the brigade through listening in through the radio communications. Could you comment on this part where it says that the Bratunac Brigade was formed from the TO units and from units of the local communes? Could you please tell us what you know about that.

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, we knew about the formation of the Bratunac Brigade through the conversations that we were monitoring. When we are talking about the TO, which was present in the local communes in their villages, they comprised a part of that brigade but forming powerful strong brigades in those areas. Analysing what we were listening to, we came to the conclusion that they had five battalions as part of that brigade. The first one was located in Bratunac itself. The second in Bjelovac, the third in Kravica. The fourth in Sase, and the fifth one was located in Fakovici. It's a little bit further away from Bratunac. The 2nd Battalion and the 4th Battalion of course were interesting to us, Sase and Bjelovac, because they were attacking the areas of Likari at that area as well as Pirici and Podloznik where our people were.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just one clarification. Speaking about what you heard through the radio communications you mentioned that you found out about the existence of the Bratunac Brigade, and did I hear you right that you also said that you found out about the existence of an assault brigade? I didn't see that on transcript.

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We found out about it at the same time probably the -- that was what the establishment was like at the time. This assault brigade, as far as we could understand, was active on a broader area of that region.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like you to look at the eighth paragraph of this document. The system of fire is organised well. Hardware and units have been assigned their firing tasks, and single mines or groups of mines have been planted in front of the positions. Could you please comment on this part of the document? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They received considerably larger quantities of artillery weapons after the formation of the brigade, we knew that they began to receive howitzers, cannons, they already had some tanks but this was strengthened from that period with some artillery and motorised units. We knew exactly from the reports of our scouts who would go a bit closer exactly where these artillery units were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you had any information from the scouts from Piricko Brdo regarding the area that they were able to see?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They frequently reported back to us. Midhat Salihovic would report back to us that they couldn't stand the pressure there anymore from the artillery fire, from the direction Jovanovici, Bjelovac, Kunjarac, Sikirici, that it was terrible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document be given an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document, which consists of two pages in the B/C/S version and two pages in the English version, ERN number 04358093 and 8094, is being tendered, received and marked as Defence Exhibit D766. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now I would like the witness to look at some footage from the Prosecution Exhibit P317. It's video number 3937, and it's the ceremony on the formation of the Bratunac Brigade on the 14th of November, 1992. We would like to show two short excerpts but we would like them both to have one exhibit number. We don't want them treated separately.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, please, could you please look at the first clip and look at it carefully and comment on it, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malagic, first, could you please tell us whether you recognise the voice of this person and do you know anything about what you have just seen on this clip?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a voice that we had heard many times. This is the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, Borivoje Tesic. When he would communicate, he would always ask to speak with the battalion commanders. He didn't want to speak with anyone else. By his voice we knew that it was an arrogant person. The commanders talked about him. They knew he had come from Vukovar, and they would say that, laughing, as they were saying it, that he would turn Srebrenica into another Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the second clip now, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malagic, do you know this man and can you comment on this clip? Have you heard -- had you heard this voice before?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this man before or heard his voice. He's talking about the strength of the battalion located at Sase, and that they would be the first ones to liberate Serb Srebrenica. I don't know why it would be Serb because the Muslims were in a majority there. As for the strength of the battalion in Sase, we really felt that on our own backs, those of us who were at Likari. We know very well how -- what its strength was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could these two video clips be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in one matter certainly don't object to the first video clip. I think the witness has recognised the name of the person and has given valuable testimony as to his interpretation. It appears to me on the second video clip he is commenting on something that was said on that video clip and did not recognise any of the persons within the video clip. I would just want to state that for the record and if there would be objection for its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a submission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have to give it an exhibit number because we haven't given it an exhibit number as yet. Do we give the exhibit number to the entire -- do you want to give the exhibit number to the entire video recording or just these clips? In other words, for your purposes, are you going to tender the entire video which will then become part of the evidence in its entirety, or only the extracts that we have seen?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me for interrupting. I've just Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. been informed by my case manager and it might assist Madam Vidovic this is already in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have that impression too but that's -- let's put it like this: Now that you are confirming it, it clarifies things for me but -- but I had that impression but I wasn't quite sure. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is quite extensive video material and it already has an exhibit number that I mentioned. What I would like is to have these two clips as one exhibit by the Defence, as one Defence Exhibit. The entire footage is something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So I need the references, the beginning and the end of each of these two video recordings. Could we go through them?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can do that during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then we can say it into the transcript. At this moment I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And the two extracts together will become Defence Exhibit D767. I asked you the question because in the back of my mind, I had a vivid recollection that this had been tendered already. Now, if you were going to make use of the entire video recording, I wanted to alert to you the fact that if the Prosecution is finding it useful, you ought to make up your mind whether you wanted the entire video or the extracts only and now it's clear. All right. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one question relating to this, Witness: This second clip that you saw, you heard that the man was talking about a strong battalion in Sase. What you know, does what you already know confirm what this man said in the video?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I do confirm that there was a strong battalion in Sase.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness Exhibit D76, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a directive from the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska of the 19th of November 1992, signed by Lieutenant General Ratko Mladic. I would like to draw your attention to page 00876282.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the English translation, this is on page 5, the last paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, have you found it? This is passage D. And it states: "The Drina Corps, from its present positions, its main forces shall persistently defend Visegrad, Zvornik and the corridor while the rest of its forces in the broader Podrinje region shall exhaust the enemy, inflect the heaviest possible losses on him and force him to leave the Birac, Zepa and Gorazde areas together with the Muslim population. First offer the able-bodied and armed men to surrender and if they refuse, destroy them." Witness, please, I would like to ask you: The Birac area, is that the area where you were living, your broader area where you were?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the broader area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the 19th of November, 1992. Could you explain, please, to the Trial Chamber whether, according to what you saw and experienced, this order by the commander of the army of Republika Srpska, General Ratko Mladic, was implemented in practice?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This directive was implemented in practice. At the time we were in a hopeless situation on their -- in their communications it all boiled down to destroying the balijas, that's the term that they used, push them towards Srebrenica and create a kind of concentration camp there. At that time, we were in the most serious situation out of that whole period, and then onwards from the month of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher now show the witness another document? It's a new document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's a document of the Bratunac Brigade command, dated the 20th of November, 1992. It's a report for the 20th of November, 1992 sent to the Drina Corps command, signed by Lieutenant Colonel Borivoje Tesic, and it bears the number 04362987. Mr. Malagic, first of all, I would like to draw your attention to what is described in item 1: "The enemy occasionally opened fire in an attempt to provoke our forces. They are still trying to infiltrate civilians to look for food. The roads are closed." Mr. Malagic, this part of the document that I just read out to you, does it reflect the actual situation in the ground where you were?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It does reflect the actual situation in this period. Civilians were not able to pass through to our villages to get food. We warned them about it but they simply continued to go because they were so hungry. Very few of them would come back once they left. They knew they couldn't pass through but they still continued to go and look for food. This was the most critical time out of that whole period, and I know that a person called Rifet Civic [phoen] died of starvation and he was from my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 4 now. It states: "We are expecting the Vukovar men to arrive any day now. After preparations in the field, we will carry out detailed reconnaissance and then launch an attack in the direction of Konjevic Polje. We will inform you later about the date on which the unit will be engaged." And then could you please look at paragraph 5, which states: "I would like you as the commander to help me and persist with a General Mynaksf to transfer the 7th Novi Sad Volunteer Company to the territory of Bratunac. The company commander, Lieutenant Goran Stoparic, Sidja expressed the wish to fight under my command. It is a company of -- numbering 130 Serbian soldiers fully equipped with weapons and equipment, BST, and mortars, and experienced in fighting in Bosnia. I will transport the troops in two buses. I hope that the arrival of such a company, even temporarily, would greatly improve the morale of the Bratunac Brigade and would yield visible results." Mr. Malagic, did you have any information about what is said in this document about the arrival of units from Serbia to the Bratunac area at the time?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, their intention was to destroy us utterly. That's why they brought in new reinforcements. They were especially happy - and we heard this - when battalions from Krajina arrived. People from Vukovar. Because they were all experienced fighters from the war theatre in Croatia. They kept arriving and attacking us. Their intention was destroy us completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know what their intentions were and how do you know about their arrival? Where does your information come from?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I just said, we had radio equipment. At that time, it was worth more to us than a mortar might have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So did you hear that through radio communications?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We listened to them saying all those things over the radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document which consists of two pages, one being a translation in English of the other, with ERN number 04362987 is being given Defence Exhibit number D768.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malagic, at that time, listening in to those communications, did you hear anything that concerned you especially and that had to do with the way these forces were equipped?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We learned that these battalions were getting mechanised and armoured squads and this upset our fighters.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now show the witness another new document? It's another document issued by the command of the Bratunac Brigade dated the 9th of December, 1992. It bears the title delivery of information, or rather, data for operative records. And it's addressed to the command of the Drina Corps. It's signed by Lieutenant Colonel Borivoje Tesic, and the ERN number is 04361559.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the document?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will read first from paragraph 2 of this document. It says: "The unit has five infantry battalions, one of which is a company strength battalion, Fakovici." In connection with this, as you have already confirmed to us that you knew about these five infantry battalions, one of which was located in Bjelovac and Sase, did you say that?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As regards this tank, did you mention artillery weapons in Bjelovac and Sase?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from these armoured mechanised units, we can see on this list what they had. They started bringing in howitzers to locations closer to Piricko Brdo. Here we have 105-millimetre howitzer. This is a highly destructive weapon, and it was facing Likari in the Sase area, and on Tablja. Midhat Salihovic and our men in Pirici told us that they had seen a howitzer in Jovanovici. And do you see these guns here, these are mountain guns, ZIS. These are all various guns. There is a difference between howitzers and the guns. And they were located in the Andrici area, targeting Likari directly. In the area of Jovanovici and Sikirici, they also had such weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we knew this very well. As I've already explained we were able to see Sase. We had several pairs of binoculars and our scouts could come close, they could creep up and see this, and I could also recognise the sound of these weapons. I had been through military training in the former JNA, so I could tell the difference in sound between a howitzer, a gun or a tank firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: 120-millimetre mortar battery is mentioned here. Do you know where this was located?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Part of this battery, because a battery comprises many artillery weapons, was located in the Gradina-Sase area, another one in the Tablja-Pobrdje area, and one in Kunjarac-Bjelovac. They had deployed several artillery weapons in each of these locations, so they were able to cover the entire territory with mortars.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about Andrici?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, in Andrici it was mainly guns that were placed there, and they could fire directly at the houses in Likari. A gun shoots directly. It has high initial targeting speed and it can destroy a house right away, unlike a howitzer which can also shoot at targets that are not visible from that position.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as Bjelovac is concerned, did you or did you not have any knowledge of the existence of artillery weapons there, and if so, where?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the broader area of Bjelovac, that is Jovanovici, Sikiric, behind the primary school in Bjelovac, there was also an 82-millimetre mortar battery there. In Jovanovici, there was a howitzer. And in Sikirici, there were also mountain guns, B1 and ZIS, targeting houses in Pirici and Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you get this information, you personally?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received this information from our men in Pirici, and many people when they went looking for food had to go through the village of Bajici while on their way down to Biljaca and they would see that. They had a good view in the direction of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now look at the last part of this document where it says, T55, T34, OTM, 60, and self-propelled weapon. Did you have any knowledge about the existence of these artillery pieces in your area and, if so, where were they positioned?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: T55, those are tanks, as well as T34; those were also tanks. Then there is M60 armoured personnel carriers and four BBPs and two self-propelled guns. This operative information corresponds to the situation on the ground. In the Bjelovac area, as far as we know, there was one tank and two armoured personnel carriers covering the area. They were moving around. They had the same kind of equipment in the Sase area to cover the area towards Likari and Potocari. They had one tank and two armoured personnel carriers in that area as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, this document will become Defence Exhibit D769. It consists of two pages in the B/C/S and two pages in the corresponding English translation, ERN number 04361559. Just for the record, the Trial Chamber points out that in paragraph numbered 3, there is a discrepancy in between the two versions in the number of M53 light machine-guns. In the B/C/S it is 103 of these machine-guns, while in the English translation, this has -- shows up as 130. Doesn't make much difference but it's only for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. For your information, yesterday, because these are all official translations, I asked them to pay attention to all the details Your Honour observed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malagic, I will now ask you something else. Yesterday and today, you described in detail military units and weapons in the areas of Bjelovac, Kunjarac, Sikiric, Pobrdje and so on. In connection with this, I will ask you the following: If someone were to say that the inhabitants of Bjelovac, Sikiric, Sase and the entire Bjelovac area from the beginning of the war until mid-December 1992, had only village guards, on the basis of your experience, would this be true?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. That claim would not hold water. They had village guards in 1991 while there was a war going on in Croatia. Later on -- I'm from Voljavica, I didn't leave of my own free will. Those units drove us out of our area. Those were assault units, assaulting Likari, Pirici, Poloznik. Such a claim would be absolutely incorrect and not grounded in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to call those units village guards in Bjelovac, Sikiric and Sase, in spite of this, and if they were to say that they had nothing to do with the Serbian army and received no assistance from the Serbian army, would this be correct?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be incorrect. Yesterday you showed me a document in which it can clearly be seen that the garrison in Bratunac was appointing Dragan Ilic from Bjelovac as company commander. The Bratunac garrison appointed him. This means that they had a well-developed command and control system at the time. The units in Bjelovac and Sase were assault units of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher please show the witness the following document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the Drina Corps command dated the 11th of December, 1992. It's a combat report addressed to the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska, and the document is signed by Colonel Milutin Skocajic. The number is 04268444. I will quote the first two paragraphs of point 2, which read as follows: "Our forces, on the night between the 10th and the 11th of December, 1992, our forces, in all sectors, zones of responsibility, set up ambushes and reconnoitred the terrain. As a result, 15 enemy combatants were killed and another one was captured. Units designated to carry out operations are making preparations and scouting the terrain." Mr. Malagic, do you remember the events linked to any ambushes in the first half of December 1992, and have you heard of any of those killings mentioned in the document I read out?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We knew very well about the setting up of these ambushes and that 15 enemy combatants were killed. These were civilians in the areas of Biljaca or Prisoj, and this prisoner here I know his name, Sead Masic, a young boy from Voljavica who was captured at the time. We knew about those ambushes but it was not possible to prevent people from going to look for food.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A bit lower down, under 3, I quote, it says: "Decision to continue with the implementation of the earlier decision on further operations, the reception of troops coming as reinforcements, the preparation of units for living, working and executing tasks in winter conditions, setting up ambushes on the axis of potential enemy incursions and sending out our reconnaissance groups to collect information about the enemy." Here in this part of the document, he speaks of preparation for the carrying out of active operations. Did you have any knowledge that attacks were being planned against you in mid-December 1992 or not?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We knew about these preparations. It was difficult to communicate with the other groups in the area. Sometimes somebody from Gostilj would come by and they would pass on the information to their groups. We tried to let our people know, but it was very difficult to pass through. It was dangerous. People often disappeared on those roads. We were then in the most difficult situation and we knew we were facing total extinction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may this document of the Drina Corps command of the 11th of December, 1992 be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- version with ERN number 04268444 and two pages for the corresponding translation into English being tendered and received and marked as Defence Exhibit D770.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malagic, how did you in Likari respond to this information that you heard on the radio that a Serb offensive was being planned, a Serb attack?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, our leader was Zajko Alic, because on the 12th of July, Osman Malagic had been killed. After that, it was Zajko Alic who was our leader. He was from Voljavica. He was an eminent man, a teacher, an educated man. He called us together. He was visibly upset. He said, "We won't be able to survive this. We have to do something. We learned of deaths of starvation among our people on a daily basis. He said we had to break through to our villages before the new year, that we had to remove those Serb strongholds, where they were constantly killing us from, Sase, Kunjarac, in order to be able to return to Voljavica, Zaluzje and Biljaca and simply to survive in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell Their Honours those people, those refugees in the woods, were they still there? Those thousands of people?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Winter found them in the area of Pirici and Poloznik. It was even worse than it had been at the beginning. People from the village would take children in to spend the night, but all those people were in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Alic, did he, when he said you had to do something, did he contact anybody else and was any help promised?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said that other people had promised to help us to return to our villages, because people saw what kind of situation we were in.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he mention anyone specifically?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He mentioned that he had met Semso Husic, the leader of a group of fighters in Poloznik. He was a man we held in high regard because he had helped us while we were stationed in Poloznik. Semso asked him, Zajko, to send us an anti-tank weapon, an anti-armour weapon, because where we were, a tank would come and destroy one house after the other. This was promised. In Likari, we had captured two hand-held mortars and two Zoljas, that is an anti-armour weapon, and he asked that a mortar be sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the person who took this hand-held mortar?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As Semso had helped my parents in Poloznik quite a lot, I volunteered, with Juso Cvrk, and we said we would take it to Semso and put ourselves at his disposal because we had been trained to use that weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the day when you went to see Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jusic, yes, that was the 13th of December. We set out at around 10.00. It's a long road. And in the evening we arrived in the Poloznik area and we reported to Semso Husic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Husic. Very well. And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, very early on the 14th of December, Semso gave us three armed men as an escort and he sent us to the Piricko Brdo area, the hill there, and from there, we could see where the camp [as interpreted] was coming from and we improvised an ambush. So that should the tank set out in the direction of Poloznik, we could destroy it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the record, it says "camp" instead of "tank." What did you say you could see from the foot of Pirici hill?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the shelter we were in, from the area of Pirici hill we could see all of Jovanovici. The river Loznicka and part of Bjelovac, as far as the school, from where we were, because there is a hill. It's quite high, and it has a lot of elevations there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the usher could show the witness the map we used yesterday, D757.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose you better leave it there in front of the witness until he finishes. Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please point out to the Trial Chamber the bottom of the Pirici hill and describe what you saw in the early morning hours on the 14th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pirici is here. That's a populated settlement, inhabited settlement. And all of this is a wooded area. It's a hilly area. We were somewhere here. And we could see very well these houses in Jovanovici, in Loznicka Rijeka and some of the houses in Bjelovac, near the school, to be more precise. So we could see all of these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Malagic, you said that you got there and took up shelter with several people there. Were you the only person who got there that day according to your information or were there any other fighters, for example, who were located above you?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see too many people. I know that above me there was an anti-aircraft machine-gun situated above me and this was manned by people from Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, immediately in your vicinity, there were people from Pirici?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Because that was their sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were armed. A PAM was hidden behind some trees.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, where did those people from Pirici get that PAM from; do you know?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They captured it in the fighting around Pirici because we didn't have anyone to give us arms or we couldn't manufacture anything. Well, you know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did they capture it from?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They captured that in the fighting around Pirici with the Serbs because there was some fierce fighting there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that morning, the 14th of December, and whether there was any shooting at any point or was there an attack?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At about 7.00, or a quarter past 7.00 maybe, as it was foggy, the fog had lifted, it was winter. I remember seeing very well Serb positions in front of me above the village of Jovanovici. These were entrenchments and there were some sandbags around the positions. Our PAM began to fire at those trenches. Then they returned fire. Our fighters again opened fire at them. The Serbs were surprised at first. And then they pulled back into the outlying houses in Jovanovici which were like real bunkers. They had placed sandbags around the houses and turned them into machine-gun nests. And then they really started firing at our fighters who were trying to get into those trenches.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what is Jovanovici? Could you show it on the map?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jovanovici is a part -- a hamlet of Loznicka Rijeka. It had some 15 to 17 houses perhaps. I will show where it is. There is a road here which -- this is the main road from Bjelovac to Skelani, and right here there is a road that leads towards Loznicka, and Jovanovici is in this area here. I will put a circle there. And it also is a part of some of these houses that are along the Skelani-Bjelovac road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please indicate that with a letter J?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your position, how far was that from Jovanovici?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the crow flies, it wasn't more than perhaps 300 to 400 metres. I could really estimate the distance very well. We could see the houses very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned other people in that small group of yours. Did you have anything?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a set of hunting binoculars which were given to us by Semso when he deployed us at that position. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain, why were you at that position? You said that you had an anti-armour weapon?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had a hand-held launcher with two shells. And in case of a counter-attack by the Serb forces towards Piricko Brdo and Loznik, or in case they tried to use a tank in that direction, it was our task to try and stop those armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please describe to the Trial Chamber how the fighting developed in the early morning exactly what happened?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the Serb forces withdrew to the houses, they opened fierce fire at our fighters above Jovanovici, and fierce fighting ensued for about half an hour. There was no artillery fire. Only at about 7.30 the shells started to fall, artillery or mortar shells from the direction of Bjelovac. But what surprised us was that they first shelled the houses. They were probably confused. They didn't know what was going on. They thought perhaps that our fighters had entered Jovanovici so they started to shell and then gradually to move the shelling towards our fighters and towards Podloznik and Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you also use your PAM at those houses?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The PAM had to fire at those houses. We used that the most because tremendous reinforcements were coming from the direction of Bjelovac towards Jovanovici, so the PAM was firing at those people and at the houses from which fire was being directed at our fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you have the impression that very well organised fighting was being conducted, either on the Serb side or on your side?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the beginning, they shelled their own houses. Our men started to withdraw because when the area gets shelled, people would escape, run away. Some would go back. So it was general chaos. A transporter would be firing from Bjelovac, from a PAM, they would be firing at the houses, they would be firing at us, so we would have to find better shelter so that we would not be exposed to that fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember at that time, did you know anything about Sikirici?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Shooting was heard in Sikiric, and because there weren't too many Serb houses there, they left the houses and they fled in the direction of Jovanovici and they joined these Serbs who were in the houses in Jovanovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All of this that was going on and that you are describing is -- is this something that you were able to see?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was able to see that spread in front of me, because the Pirici hill, you probably were never there, is a good point where you could see all of that. You have control of everything if you're there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show the witness Defence Exhibit 271 now, and this is an excerpt from video footage we received from the Prosecutor, and it was number 1574. We are going to hand out the -- to the Trial Chamber and to the Prosecution a transcript of this Exhibit D271.1 so you can follow the footage better.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please listen carefully to what is being shown and to what you can hear? I would like to also ask you to comment on what you hear and what you see, particularly to what you hear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malagic, based on what you have heard, could you please tell the Trial Chamber whether this is -- these are Serbs talking amongst themselves or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are Serbs talking.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions about this. At 0039, a voice said that they were urgently looking for precise coordinates. Did you hear the voice say that?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this event and can you give your own comment regarding what he said?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, they are looking for precise coordinates in order to use their artillery. They said we can't do it like this. They could see that these shells were being fired everywhere. I don't know if they were being guided or were being guided wrongly but the shells were hitting all over the place. The houses, Jovanovici, Pirici, so they said, "We can't do it like this." They have to know where the shells should be fired. And then later, they said you've heard about the coordinates, fire at the part above Jovanovici. That's where we were. And our fighters. So above Jovanovici, he noticed that and he was already giving them the coordinates. Up until that time they were shooting blindly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's stop at Jovanovici now. The voice said, "Go up," meaning above me, above Jovanovici, around here, above Jovanovici, take those coordinates, you have the map. Let them target and fire there. Then he cursed. And then he said they should fly up there, they should do something. Did I understand you properly that the PAM that you mentioned, it was above Jovanovici?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, our PAM was at the Pirici hill all the time, above Jovanovici so they could sense that it was firing at the houses where they were firing at us from so they tried to neutralise that also.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I would also like to ask you the following: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber exactly what a PAM is and does it have anything characteristic as a weapon?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A PAM is an abbreviation for a Protivavionski Mitraljez anti-aircraft machine-gun, and it's usually placed on a vehicle. There are browning models. And its specific action is that in the series of bullets it fires, every 12th bullet is an incendiary bullet, in order to be able to set the plane on fire if it happens to hit an airplane.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Before this incident, did you have any experience before in fighting, actually before this event with that type of weapon? I mean, did you have any experience in using that kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very often, when a PAM is fired, we hide well because if it hits something, that weapon has lots of shrapnel, so if it hits hay, it will set the hay on fire. If it hits the house, it will set the house on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At 113 they said they are about to take off, and then the next section says it means from Kunjarac towards Pirici. Could you comment on this, please?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the first flyover by the planes. And this reference from Kunjarac towards Pirici on the right side, I can actually show that to you on the map. It's in the sector of Ljuljaska. I will mark that with an X. This is where very many of our civilians were concentrated, and they were waiting for the outcome of the fighting in order to be able to go down to Biljaca, Voljavica and Zaluzje. There was a large crowd of people there. The airplane saw them out in the open, and they really -- it really massacred the population. They thought that the plane would not fire at them, that it was going towards Pirici, but they were spotted out in the open so that many, many civilians were killed who were only actually wanting to go back to their villages. I don't know if the actual pilot of the plane was aware of what it had -- what he had done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. For the record, the witness has marked an X -- marked with an X on the map a spot which is within an imaginary triangle between -- of -- composed of Jasovac, Sase and Podloznik. Yes. Go ahead Madam Vidovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have one more question on this topic. This airplane, was it flying over other regions as well where you were?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was constantly flying over Kunjarac and Jovanovici and Pirici, Podloznik, then in the direction of Voljavica where there was also fighting. It was flying over that entire area. Actually two airplanes were covering that entire area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, you could hear Mungos and Kokara being mentioned on this footage. Do you know anything about this? Are these Serbs or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mungos, his last name is Prodanovic. I don't know what his first name is. I know that before the war he was working at a ticket conductor in the local bus, and they also had a unit called Mungos, but he was also called Mungos. The other thing is that Kokara was working at the OKA combine in Kravica before the war. He knew a lot of martial arts, and he also had a special group with him that was active in that area of Bjelovac, Kunjarac, Sase and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You described these two people. Could you please tell us whether they were Muslims or Serbs?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to show the witness another video clip. It's a Defence Exhibit D111, and I would also like to mention that this is an excerpt from Prosecution Exhibit P317, and it also refers to Bjelovac. Would you please play it from 00 to 0101?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Witness, could you please carefully look at the footage and also follow what is being said? Can we play the video, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, do you remember this plane flying over? Is that the plane that you described as flying over Jovanovici on the 9th, in the morning? Actually, on the 14th of December, 1992 or not?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's that same airplane.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you register a voice saying, did you see the planes shooting, that word, prokati [phoen], shooting? Can you explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means killing, destroying, causing havoc.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then, it says, and did you see how well they are firing? And the second voice asks, where is the other one? Do you recall that on that morning, right after 9.00, there were several airplanes, more than one?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the second airplane.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That's a bit of a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Rephrase your question. I'm just asking to you rephrase it because --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, but it's just that the witness already mentioned these two airplanes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, did you already mention that there were two planes flying over that morning?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that there were two, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I will pay attention to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice a voice saying, "Now they are firing from a machine-gun?" And then the second one said, "Well they are firing at it but they didn't hit it." Do you remember whether the PAM that you were talking about fired or didn't fire at the airplane?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it had to shoot at the airplane. Whenever it would come in the direction of our positions, the PAM would fire at it but it didn't hit it. Also, the infantry unit fighters were also firing but it wasn't effective. As far as the second plane is concerned, it came later. It was an agricultural airplane from ADA. But the second plane was a much more modern airplane. It was a G4 Gallet airplane, and you could see very well what it was. It came from the direction of Serbia. There was an airfield there, Ponikve, near Titovo Uzice. I served in the army there, so I knew about that airport. It came and it was armed with air-to-surface missiles, and it was more active in Voljavica and Kunjarac, whereas the other plane was firing exclusively in Jovanovici and the positions of our fighters around Pirici and Voljavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what is your comment on this, "If there are Ustashas there, they are crazy." Could you please comment on that? First of all, who are Ustashas?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs called us Muslims by that name, Ustashas, as well as Croatian Catholics. That's how they called us. And when it says "if there are Ustashas there, they must be crazy," well, you need to experience what it's like to have the air force fire at you. They really would need to be crazy to be in the area where these explosive devices or the -- these bombs are being dropped. There is a lot of smoke that they generate, and these are large amounts of explosives with a large number of shrapnel which are deadly, and nobody who is in that area can stay alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at this last scene on the video footage? Do you see it? Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that houses are burning on that image? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see, not -- not all the houses are burning, there is smoke from the bombs being dropped from the plane. And then in the right part of the photograph, you can see that there is a house that's burning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what exactly is this place that we are seeing? Where is this image?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the part where Loznicka Rijeka and Jovanovici start. It's a part near the road. You don't see the main part of Jovanovici. You see this part of Jovanovici towards the woods and Loznicka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, it's nevertheless Jovanovici?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a couple of houses to the right, you can see them, that's where Loznicka Rijeka begins, and there are no more houses there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this. Are these the houses at which your PAM was firing too?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the houses that they were firing from. These were proper machine-gun nests that they were firing from. And then you can see our fighters were up higher, and they were firing -- they were firing from an M53 machine-gun, whereas our fighters were shooting at those houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber how these houses were set on fire?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever would tell you how they were set on fire would be lying. It could have happened from the shooting from our PAM. Whoever said that they knew exactly how they were set on fire would not be telling the truth. It could have been our PAM. It could have been the Serb artillery shooting from across the Drina. It could have been the bombs dropped from the airplane. So these are the three causes for the fire in those houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you would not be able to tell the exact cause?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been any of these three things that I mentioned. Nobody could tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How long were you there on that day?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in that area until the afternoon, until 4.00 in the afternoon to be exact.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did the planes continue to fly over throughout that time?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please play the rest of this footage from 0400 up to 503.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please carefully look and listen to what these people are saying?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, did you notice a male voice saying, "Wait, it wasn't burning before now." And then a younger male voice said, "The plane just bombed it. It dropped about ten bombs just now." I would like to ask you the following. In your testimony yesterday you said that from your positions where you were observing the events from, you were able to see a part of Bjelovac. Were you able to see it from the shelter where you had moved to? You said that you had gone a little bit more back.

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to see the whole of Bjelovac. I could see up to the elementary school. This other part, near Loznicka Rijeka, I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, did I understand you properly as saying that you were able to see this other part of Bjelovac that you could see on the footage?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not Bjelovac. There was no fighting in Bjelovac. If you look on the map where you see Bjelovac, I will mark exactly the part up until the fighting -- until -- up where the fighting reached. I will point to that part. There is a letters SK indicating where the school was. Actually, there was no fighting in that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing this bombing that the voices are talking about on the -- in the footage?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw all of the bombing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm speaking about this specific bombing that we showed in this footage. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber so that it's quite clear, which part was bombed? Which place? Which hamlet?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point, a part of Loznicka Rijeka was bombed between Bjelovac and Jovanovici. That was the part that was bombed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ahead.

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was strange to us at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, when this was happening, were you able to conclude why they were bombing this area?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially we thought perhaps there were ammunition depots in the houses and they were afraid they might fall into Muslim hands. That's what we thought. But we had no idea actually why they were bombing Loznicka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever learn more about this after these events?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Around the 23rd of December, when the fighting died down in that area, a relative of mine, Haris Ahmetovic from Mihaljevici, told us that together with a small group of brave fighters, he had tried to enter Loznicka Rijeka from the direction of the Drina and there they clashed with special purpose units, the Mungos and Kokara that were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the comment you can hear on this video?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These people are saying a group has gone to surround those Ustasha that came from the direction of the Drina, and probably that was why they bombed those houses. You heard the comment this house was not in flames. And then you could hear them saying that the plane had dropped about ten bombs on those houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the dropping of those ten bombs on Loznicka Rijeka, you personally?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see each and every bomb. We called them boilers. They were bombs packed with explosives, highly destructive. Probably of Yugoslav manufacture. Q.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I think we can have a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have a 25 or 30-minute break, depending on what your answer is going to be. I have a feeling that you're approaching the end of your direct. How much more time do you think you require?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the next part of the session certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And are you in a position to start your cross-examination today?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there were several things that were brought up that we would like to discuss with our colleagues, and we might just ask the Trial Chamber to bear with us and start tomorrow or just start a very minimum today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Please try and give us a more definitive picture when we come back after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can have a 30-minute break, actually. Also, in the meantime, we are going to meet to discuss several matters related to this case and other cases. So we will let you know if we are planning to start later than 30 minutes. All right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers, are you in a position now to inform us whether you would be starting your cross-examination today?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will start today after the next break and then the bulk of course of my cross-examination will be in tomorrow's session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long do you anticipate roughly your cross-examination to last?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it will last probably one court day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the witness is scheduled to leave when? Madam Registrar? Perhaps we could check a little bit because I wouldn't like to keep him -- in other words, when you say one whole court day, that would exclude today's part or not? In other words, if tomorrow we start at 10.00 and finish at quarter to 2.00, would you be in a position to conclude? We will have one break.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That's what I was going to ask. It depends on -- normally when we have the modified court day, we have less breaks, and I believe during that time period, if we would follow modified breaks, I should be able to conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to keep the witness here for more than he is actually scheduled to be. So Madam Vidovic, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I continue examining the witness, I wish to state for the record that during the break we checked the time needed to locate the video material, and I can say that both video clips come from P317, one of two videos. The first video clip, called Tesic, is on 0107048 to 010837 of the original video. And the second video clip is from 0103025 to 010400 of the original video, P317.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. And please, could we have this part cut, pasted and printed out for our secretaries so that they could give it the exhibit number that we indicated earlier on, which I think is 767, D767. All right. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, before the break, we were talking about the location where there was fighting, and you said it was in Jovanovici and Loznicka Rijeka. While you were there, and you said you were there on the 14th of December, in the area overlooking Jovanovici until about 4.00 p.m., did a single armed Muslim manage to the best of your knowledge to enter Jovanovici and Loznicka Rijeka except for the group you mentioned from the direction of Pirici?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, at one point in time, was there a counter-attack by the Serb forces, a strong counter-attack on that day?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When they had consolidated their ranks, starting from 8.00, help arrived in Jovanovici from Bjelovac for them and they started pushing back our fighters towards Pirici and Loznik. Their counter-attack lasted the whole day, especially those two groups, the Mungos and the Kokara that we mentioned, who fought that group, and pushed them back towards Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was happening at the same time in Kunjarac?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At Kunjarac, there was also fierce fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that someone you knew well was killed on that day?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At around 4.00 in the afternoon, we withdrew to the area of Poloznik, our whole group, and there I learned of the death of Semso Husic who had been killed at Kunjarac, and this upset me. I had a very good opinion of that young man. He was the local leader of the people in Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you stay in Poloznik or did you go somewhere else on that day or the following day?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't stay in Poloznik. I wanted to know what had happened in my village of Voljavica. With all due respect to the other villages, I was born in Voljavica and I wanted to go there. So Huso and I set out towards Voljavica along the Poloznik-Ljuljaska-Bilisnjik [phoen]-Prisoj road. And we met our leader Zajko in Zalasnik [phoen] and the other men.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before you left this area, did you learn what had happened in Kunjarac? Did you have any information about any weapons that may or may not have been captured there?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew that there was fighting going on there, around Kunjarac. We knew from before that the Serbs had a stronghold there, a very strong one, that they had a special purpose platoon there, parts of the Krajina Battalion. They guarded Kunjarac well because their water pumps were there for the Bratunac waterworks, city waterworks, and this was one of their biggest strongholds in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say the reds were there, do you mean the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reds were a special unit and the Red Berets were a different unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. When you went off towards Voljavica on the 14th of December, what was happening there? Was there any fighting there?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We met with our leader, Zajko. We met up with him. They were happy that we were still alive. He told us there had been fighting with the Red Berets all day. The Red Berets had attacked Voljavica. And that they had managed to inflict losses on the Red Berets and to capture some rifles and ammunition. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can the witness now be shown two Defence exhibits, D94 and D95? Can they be shown to the witness together.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, would you please have a look at D94? It's a record of soldiers' deaths. The number is 01321081, and it's about Cvijic, son of Ilija. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the date and place of his death? It says in Voljavica, on the 14th of December 1992, killed in battle, unit Red Berets. Please look at the place where this person was born?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Novi Sad Zabilje?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's in Yugoslavia. That's a different state.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at this other record sheet now, Radovan Djukic. Son of Jeposava [phoen]. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see his place of birth?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Pakrac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the date and place of death?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: 14th of December, 1992, wounded. And then it says died on the 8th of January at the Military Medical Academy in Belgrade. Do you see the unit, 2nd Infantry Battalion, Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this correspond to what you were told by Zajko?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's evident here that the Red Berets were fighting in the area of Voljavica with our men from Voljavica and that some were killed in that fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the leader of your group, Zajko, tell you this, that they fought with them?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that the Red Berets had participated in the attack on Voljavica and that many had been killed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I may add, if I had been killed in Voljavica my parents would why I had been killed defending my village. I don't know what their motive was to fight for my house and my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your clarification, Witness. Would you please now look at a video? This is P317, two out of two. This is the second part of the video. And it's dated the 15th of December, 1992. And could you please stop at 1408.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, you can take a good look at this picture. Do you recognise this area?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Voljavica, my village. I recognise this big house. It's Ago Suljagic's [phoen] house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone in this picture? And if you do, could you indicate that to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the person facing us. His name is Goran, known as Gera. He's from a nearby Serbian village called Sikiric, and you can see that he's holding a Motorola. I knew this man well before the war. He was a good football player. And I played in the local soccer club, and we often met at football games.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please continue playing the tape until 1458.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unfortunately, we were unable to get hold of a transcript. We will do so but I will not put many questions about the content of the conversation. I will simply ask the witness:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this man being introduced as Svetozar Andric, the commander of the assault brigade?

utterances.speaker: AZIR MALAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we just heard on the tape.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment because I wasn't anticipating this. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, without having a transcript, there is no way at this point in time that we can understand what is the content, whether the question is being directed to the contents and can be answered properly by the witness, and I would state that if the witness can say something about just the image, I think that might be permissible. But at this point to go into the content --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I would have also preferred the question to have been a little bit different, asking the witness whether he recognised this person, whether he knew him. But the problem that Ms. Sellers has indicated is basically our problem as well. Because we don't know what this person is supposed to have said. So on the other hand, we have seen this before, and it's a rough guess that I'm making but I would imagine that if we have seen it already, as we certainly have, because I remember it, there probably -- there is in existence already a transcript in English. So if we could dig that up and put ourselves in a situation where we can follow or at least find out what this gentleman with the cap on his head has just said, it will be -- it will put us in a position where we can follow and understand at least. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, of course, we will get the transcript. We talked to the witness until late the night before yesterday, but what can be of assistance is to play the video back and to ask the interpreters to interpret what is said here, if you feel it can be of assistance, or we can get the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I could easily live with that and I'm sure my two colleagues could live with that too, but I don't know whether you would --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would have no objection to that. I guess there would be a question in terms of what was said at what point. We see that there is no indication of the timing. I think that's a very practical solution that we certainly could go forward with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it there are going to be questions on the substance of the words said by this person on the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I only put a question to the witness as to whether he heard that this person was introduced as Svetozar Andric, the commander of the assault brigade. I will put no other questions about the content at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
